problems.description:
The client is looking for a technical development team with experience in AI applications, knowledge bases, data engineering, and full-stack product development to co-build an AI shopping assistant.

The project already has a real business foundation:
- A Xiaohongshu (RED) account with 30,000+ followers
- Tens of thousands of shopping consultations answered to date
- A consumer data knowledge base system covering multiple brands, categories, and consumption scenarios
- Ongoing daily responses to real shopping questions in fan groups
- Existing integration with relevant B-side data operations

The product's core capabilities include:
- Identifying brand quality and safety risks
- Assessing whether brand marketing content is compliant
- Recommending high-value, quality brands and products
- Providing trustworthy and easy-to-understand consumer education

The product will serve two types of scenarios in the future:
1. C-side: Assisting users in making consumption and shopping decisions through AI Search, Chatbot, or Agent.
2. B-side: Providing structured data API services to AI search, intelligent customer service, Agents, and other data operations.

The 100 USD bounty for this round is for the first-phase technical solution and collaboration evaluation. A complete product delivery is not expected within this budget. The full development scope, timeline, and budget will be negotiated separately after the team is selected.

Participating teams are asked to submit:
- An overall product and technical architecture proposal
- A data governance, update, and quality control plan for the consumer knowledge base
- MVP scope for the C-side shopping assistant and B-side data API
- A plan covering model, retrieval, recommendation, risk identification, and result traceability
- Development phases, staffing, timeline, and budget estimates
- Team introduction and relevant case studies in AI, knowledge bases, recommendation systems, or data products
- Suggestions for ongoing collaboration

The client's original knowledge base or sensitive user data will not be provided at this stage. A separate confidentiality and data usage agreement can be signed once formal collaboration begins.
problems.title: 【Seeking a Tech Development Team】AI Shopping Assistant: Consumer Knowledge Base-Driven Consumer-Facing Assistant and Business-Facing Data Service

Recruit students for the "Xingchen Academy AI Comic Drama Practical Entrepreneurship Training Camp · Advanced Dreamweaver Class." For every 1 student you refer who completes registration, pays tuition, and actually attends, you earn ¥1,000 (this listing price is the per-person reward; settlements are cumulative based on actual enrollment — the more you recruit, the more you earn, with no upper limit).

problems.description:
[Objective] Codify the experience of senior process engineers into software capability, achieving "model in, solution out": automatically parse forming difficulties from any die forging model, autonomously generate passes and a complete set of process parameters, run fully automated DEFORM simulation iterations, and output a defect-free, performance-compliant process plan that surpasses manual work. For standard parts, "plan generation + simulation iteration" ≤ 10 minutes, with process design efficiency improved by more than 80% over manual methods.

[Core Requirements]
1. Bidirectional data integration: No-code linkage with SolidWorks / UG-NX / CATIA / Creo (STEP/IGS/STL/PRT) and DEFORM-2D/3D; automatic read/write and batch submission of models, parameters, and simulation results.
2. Autonomous process decision-making: Using geometry, material, and mechanical properties as constraints, automatically complete forming pass breakdown (pre-forging → initial forging → finish forging → sizing), deformation distribution per pass (pre-forging 60–70% / initial forging 20–30% / finish forging 5–10%), and generation of five categories of complete process parameters (temperature / equipment / motion / auxiliary / precision).
3. Closed-loop simulation optimization: Automatically invoke DEFORM for validation, perform reverse iteration based on defects / stress-strain / dimensional deviation, score multiple plans, and output the optimal one.
4. Engineering deployability: Chinese-language visual interface, offline Windows deployment, local data encryption, retained manual intervention interface, one-click output of standardized process documents (Word/Excel/PDF/DEFORM templates).

[Delivery Phases] Phase 1: Data interface and parsing layer (8 weeks) · Phase 2: Process decision engine (core, 12 weeks) · Phase 3: Simulation iteration optimization and delivery deployment (8 weeks). Total duration approximately 7 months (partially parallel).

[Prerequisites] Party A provides ≥ 20 sets of verified historical forging process and simulation data for algorithm initialization and acceptance comparison; CAD/DEFORM licenses and hardware procurement are not included.
problems.title: Die Entwicklung eines intelligenten Systems für Gesenkschmiedeprozesse: CAD-Geometrieanalyse + geschlossener DEFORM-Simulationskreislauf + autonome Entscheidungsfindung für mehrstufige Prozesse

problems.description:
[Context]
A multi-store auto dealer group runs DMS, OEM lead portals, OA, WeCom, a call centre and an after-sales system as silos: staff re-key data, call outcomes collapse into labels like "hung up", customers leave with the salesperson, managers chase by hand. This project does **not** replace those systems - it adds an integration layer, a data hub, an AI-agent platform and four surfaces (staff app, manager app, PC console, group cockpit) on top.

[Requirements]

M1 Integration & Data Hub (P0)
1. API integration: DMS, CRM, OA, WeCom, call centre (bi-directional)
2. RPA integration: OEM lead / feedback portals - no open API but human-operable
3. File ingestion: Excel/CSV legacy customer lists, service records, training material
4. OCR / speech ingestion: call recordings, IDs, invoices, site photos
5. Hub: customer + employee masters, subject areas, metric layer, tags & profiles, data quality, data-level permissions

M2 Staff "AI Workbench" app (P0)
6. Unified work inbox aggregating all agent messages plus sales / after-sales / reporting progress
7. "My agents": one person, several roles, several bound digital staff, each with duty scope and open-task count
8. Dynamic AI task cards driven by role, live progress and business rules (never hard-coded): goal, progress, deadline, priority, suggested action
9. Voice / text / photo reporting, auto-structured
10. AI-compiled daily report across sales, after-sales, service, reception

M3 Digital Sales Officer & long-term customer ownership (P0)
11. Fast lead-response prompting (three-minute class) across all lead channels
12. Customer 360: source, target model, budget, interests, objections, history
13. Pre-call briefing: history summary, opening angle, script, objective
14. Call capture via work phone + recorder card / badge device (hardware form, pairing and recording-consent wording fixed in phase 1)
15. Transcription with rep/customer speaker separation, keywords, summary, tags, search
16. AI call review: intent, objections, sentiment, next action, coaching
17. Auto-filing into the OEM system: AI drafts, **employee confirms**, then RPA/API writes back
18. Cross-cycle customer memory, follow-up cadence, rep hand-over without context loss

M4 After-sales officer & service-job assistant (P1)
19. Service call-back queue with priority, missed-call prompts, scripts
20. Appointment booking, return-to-shop prediction, churn early warning
21. Auto job dispatch after clock-in: labour-hour estimate, fault description, service history, parts suggestion, stock status
22. Start job / request parts / submit progress / upload photos - process capture and efficiency analytics

M5 Store-manager console & PC back office (P0)
23. Ops decision agent: "who is behind today, why, what do I do" returns lagging staff, root cause, recommended action, executable moves
24. Campaign orchestration: manager states the need in chat, AI completes the material checklist, flags reusable stock, dispatches tasks once confirmed
25. Store ops cockpit: call volume, effective conversations, qualified leads, showroom invitations, orders, call-backs, task completion, staff ranking, AI alerts
26. Team task & performance board: completion rates, slippage alerts, AI improvement suggestions
27. Agent configuration centre: role, job binding, task rules, reminder policy, output templates, tool permissions
28. Rules & knowledge base: sales scripts, vehicle + campaign + after-sales knowledge, prompt templates

M6 New-hire training assistant (P1) and group cockpit (P1/P2)
29. Onboarding records, training plan, simulated customer dialogue, script scoring, skill-gap analysis, pre-duty rehearsal
30. Cross-store comparison, task completion, staff efficiency, follow-up coverage, anomaly alerts, audit overview

[Non-negotiable governance]
- A digital employee = role + knowledge + task rules + tool calls + long-term memory + human review. Not a prompt.
- Critical actions (auto-filing, outreach, dispatch) always require human confirmation; no bypass path.
- Five audit log families - task, call, AI (incl. prompt version + knowledge source), filing, management - each recording actor, time, action, content, result, origin.
- Permissions tiered group / store / department / role / individual; phone numbers, IDs and recordings masked by tier.
- Model governance: monitor output quality, error rate, adoption rate, anomaly flags.

[Delivery path - ~24 weeks]
1. Requirements & prototype sign-off (w1-2): interviews, system + data + interface survey, recording-hardware decision. 2. Sales MVP (w3-8): workbench, sales officer, customer profile, call capture & review, auto-filing. 3. Manager console & PC back office (w9-14). 4. After-sales & service (w15-20). 5. Pilot and rollout plan (w21-24), 1-2 stores.

[Scope]
Upstream API surface, RPA feasibility and the recording hardware / consent model are locked in phase 1. Break your bid down by module: integration, data hub, agent platform, app surfaces, call pipeline, rollout.
problems.title: Auto Dealer Group AI Digital-Workforce Platform: Agent Workbench, Data Hub, Digital Staff & Ops Cockpit

problems.description:
[Definition] Stateful, competitor-driven Amazon product content production Agent: converts competitor ASINs, URLs, and reference images into fact-verified product intelligence, SEO Listings, 7 structurally consistent product images, A+ Content, and an advertising framework, with human review gates at key nodes. Marketplace: US. What V1 needs to prove is a **repeatable, auditable, reversible closed loop** — not a chatbot wrapped in a long prompt, and not an Amazon ERP.

[V1 Scope] Includes: input and public data collection | Product Truth Sheet and confidence levels | Listing/SEO/compliance | 7-image planning, reference image generation and local editing, visual QA | A+ plan | advertising strategy framework.
Excludes: creating or modifying Listings in Seller Central | creating ad Campaigns or adjusting prices | inventory/FBA/finance/review auto-reply | unsourced inference of non-public data such as exact sales figures or hidden backend keywords | unattended publishing.

[Requirements List]

1 | Input and Collection (P0)
- Input 2–5 competitor ASINs / URLs / main and secondary images and A+ images; optionally supplement with color, size, material, quantity, packaging, and non-modifiable structure (high-priority user declarations, still retain source and version)
- Collect ASIN, Brand, Title, Bullets, Description, A+, Product Information, Price, Rating, Review Count, Variations, BSR (only when publicly displayed on the page); store source URL, collection time, raw value, parsed value, and availability status per field
- Degradation: inaccessible / anti-scraping / regional differences → report status and reason and allow manual upload, **no fabrication**; A+ or dynamic module failure → Partial/Unavailable; price and ratings carry timestamps and must not be treated as long-term facts; multi-source conflicts → Conflict and block downstream

2 | Product Truth Sheet and Confidence Levels (P0)
- Fields: Identity / Structure / Materials / Dimensions / Package Contents / Functions-Features-Benefits / Limitations and non-modifiable items / Evidence
- Single fact entry: fact_id, claim, category, confidence, evidence, allowed_usage, status/version
- Four levels: Confirmed — usable downstream; Likely — **not publishable by default**, requires human upgrade; Uncertain — prohibited from marketing content; Conflict — blocks related claims, human selects and leaves audit trail

3 | Competitor Insights, Positioning, and Keywords (P0/P1)
- Common selling points, keyword patterns, marketing task per image, consumer pain points, content gaps, verifiable differentiation opportunities
- Core + 3–5 Supporting selling points, each with Feature → Benefit → Proof; **Proof must trace back to approved facts or real visual evidence**
- Six keyword layers: core category terms / high purchase intent / Feature / Use Case / long-tail / Backend Search Terms; when integrating third-party data (search volume, ranking, competition, CPC), the priority algorithm must show input sources and calculation logic

4 | Listing and Compliance Engine (P0/P1)
- Generate Title, Product Highlights, five bullets, Description, Backend Search Terms
- Check length, spelling, repetition and keyword stuffing; identify competitor trademarks, restricted terms, and unsupported claims; focus coverage on medical, safety, children's, absolute, performance, and compatibility claims
- **Rules must not be hardcoded into Prompts**: requires an updatable Policy Knowledge Base + rule version + effective date
- Three states: PASS — proceed / WARNING — retain risk note for human judgment / FAIL — block and provide rule, matched content, and revision suggestion

5 | 7-Image Architecture and Visual Consistency (P0, hardest part)
- Default tasks: main image / core benefit / feature explanation / usage scenario / secondary benefit / dimensions and packaging fit / lifestyle; order adjustable by category
- Per-image Brief: Objective, Consumer Question, Selling Point, Composition, Product Position, Background, Copy, Visual Hierarchy, Required Details, Forbidden Changes
- Human-approved Master Product Reference (multi-angle reference images + structural annotations + color and material samples + non-modifiable list) as conditional input; **each image input = Master + Scene Brief + Composition Brief**, not regenerated from text
- Locked items: shape, proportions, material, color, hole positions and shapes, handle, buttons, connectors, Frame, patterns, wiring, accessories, product quantity
- Per-image QA: compare against Master, PASS locks version, FAIL **redoes only the current image**, exceeds threshold → escalate to human. "Looks great but the product changed" is an immediate failure

6 | Reference Image Local Editing (P0)
- Reference-Based Editing / local masking, **separately designed** from ordinary text-to-image
- Acceptance instruction: "Only change the black mesh of the black pet bathing rack to the light blue of the reference sample" — composition, dimensions and position, hole shapes and positions, frame, connectors, accessories, animal, lighting, background, and resolution all preserved
- Save original image, edited region, color and material reference, instruction, model version, seed, and output version; non-edited region stability evaluated using pixel/perceptual difference + structural detection + human confirmation
- When the model cannot stably preserve non-target regions, it must **explicitly fail** — do not substitute "similar" for "unchanged"

7 | A+ Content Agent (P1)
- 7 modules: Hero/brand story, core benefit, feature breakdown, lifestyle, secondary selling points, dimensions and details, (optional) comparison table (only when a real product matrix exists)
- Copy, captions, and comparison fields reference the same fact library; after generation, run cross-asset consistency and compliance re-check across Listing–Images–A+

8 | Advertising Strategy Agent (P1) and Future Closed Loop (P2)
- Five Campaign types: Auto / Manual Exact / Phrase / Broad / Product Targeting; keyword pool includes Core, long-tail, Feature, Use Case, and competitor ASIN targeting
- V1 outputs strategy and structural recommendations only, **does not create Campaigns, does not adjust prices, does not promise performance**
- P2: ad data → keyword intelligence → Listing optimization → creative optimization; Winner/Potential/Losing/Search Term Opportunities classification requires recorded decision thresholds; automated actions require permissions, budget caps, cooldown periods, and human approval

9 | State Machine, Human Review Gates, and Version Control (P0)
- Each product has an independently persisted Project (Input, Competitor Data, Product Truth, Keywords, Listing, Creative, A+, Advertising, Compliance, Approvals, Version History); **must not lose data on close and reopen**
- States: INPUT_RECEIVED → COMPETITOR_COLLECTED → PRODUCT_ANALYZED → WAITING_PRODUCT_APPROVAL → PRODUCT_APPROVED → SEO_ANALYZED → LISTING_GENERATED → IMAGE_PLAN_GENERATED → WAITING_IMAGE_PLAN_APPROVAL → IMAGE_GENERATION → IMAGE_QA → APLUS_GENERATED → AD_STRATEGY_GENERATED → FINAL_QA → COMPLETE
- Four non-skippable Gates: Product Truth / Positioning / Image Architecture / Final Audit
- Retry / Regenerate / Edit / Rollback / Approve-Reject all leave an audit trail (object, version, approver, time, reason)
- **Dependency invalidation**: when an approved fact is changed, related Listing, image, A+, and ad assets are marked Stale / Needs Review and must not be silently reused

[Non-Functional] Traceable | Repeatable (modules run independently, results versioned, approved assets not overwritten) | Observable (collection/model/QA/retry/human-wait all have status, duration, and error logs) | Secure (project isolation, least privilege, credentials never enter Prompts or logs) | Cost-controlled (per-project per-module model and third-party data costs visible, supports budget and retry caps) | Maintainable (policies, rules, models, collectors, and prompt templates all version-replaceable).

[Bidding Notes] Don't lead with full automation — one incorrect fact will cascade and contaminate all assets. Don't hardcode so-called A10/Alexa weight formulas. Break down your quote by: data collection / model calls / state and versioning / review interface / QA / operations / third-party data, and explain the risks and alternatives for each item.
problems.title: Amazon Product Content Production Agent V1: Competitor Reverse Engineering → Listing → 7-Image Visual Consistency → A+ and Advertising Framework

problems.description:
[Client & context]
An Amazon boutique-model apparel seller (own factory partner), based in Shenzhen. Amazon US only for now (English is enough), Canada under consideration; two storefronts, one dominant; roughly 20 parent listings this half, about fifty to sixty variations in total; colour x size makes the SKU count explode. The team shrank to **two operators** this year and may hire again next year. They run **Lingxing ERP** (API/MCP entitlement still to be confirmed). TikTok is planned, so video demand will grow.
Core ask: use AI to carry the whole operation on a two-person team - it must run with few people, and new hires must be able to plug in quickly.

[Priority] The client is explicit: **module B (advertising) and module C (inventory) come first**. Both sides agreed on a phased build: frame first, then module by module, then continuous tuning after 3-6 months of accumulated data. Listing creation today runs off Amazon back-office templates and the client considers it a non-problem, so module A can be deferred or dropped.

[Requirements - 5 modules, 20 items]

A. Product content / creative (listing pipeline, deferrable)
1. Image generation: turn flat-lay garment shots into on-model images / virtual try-on
2. Video generation (later): groundwork for TikTok, ramping up over time
3. Listing copy pipeline: titles, five bullets, supporting copy

B. Advertising & traffic data (P0)
4. Keyword rank monitoring: organic rank position for each product keyword
5. Ad structure monitoring + ROI: campaign structure and return on ad spend
6. Daily traffic monitoring: organic vs paid split
7. Smart recommendations: operating and bidding advice generated from the monitored data
8. Business reporting: daily and weekly reports

C. Inventory & supply chain (P0)
9. Stock-out alerts: many colour/size combinations each holding little stock - flag which product is about to run out
10. Turnover analysis: which SKUs tie up cash, which sell through; combine sales trend with days-on-hand (e.g. 50 units untouched for 7/15/30 days) to decide on clearance
11. Replenishment advice: propose a plan before the stock-out lands
12. FBA allocation & packing lists: given factory intake, split it across 5 shipments with identical carton content (e.g. 5 units of black/small -> 1 per carton) and generate the packing list
13. Automatic shipment creation: once the warehouse has packed to the list, create the shipment in Amazon Seller Central from the real packing data
14. Factory purchase-order sheet: read orders, generate the standard PO sheet, and after confirmation trigger factory production and warehouse dispatch to FBA

D. After-sales & voice of customer (P1)
15. Return analysis: statistics, root cause, improvement advice
16. Negative-review management: auto-classification, issue rollup, reply assistance
17. Review collection: gather and classify all reviews and surface recurring problems

E. Finance & cost modelling (P1)
18. Per-SKU cost and profit modelling, including ad spend and storage fees
19. Excess storage fee calculation - the client called it "ECOST", which in context means Amazon excess / long-term storage fees; **the exact fee scope must be confirmed during detailing**
20. Product life-cycle decisions: for products past 100 / 120 days, compare dispose / discount and keep selling / Amazon bulk liquidation, including storage, disposal and ad cost, and recommend one

[Three implementation stages, already agreed with the client]
1. Baseline data analysis: the AI reads the data like a sharp analyst and surfaces problems
2. Inject client judgement: abstract the client's own reasoning into rules for the AI
3. Continuous tuning: after 3-6 months of data, let the AI find more

[Open items - the poster is chasing these; they do not block bidding]
1. Whether Lingxing ERP API / MCP access is enabled and whether it costs extra
2. GMV / revenue level, promised by the client, to size the project
3. Budget - the client has given no figure yet (they believe price should track service and results); comparable market quotes are around CNY 5,000 and our framework quote around CNY 10,000. **The final budget for this order is to be agreed once scope is locked**
4. What "ECOST" / excess storage fee concretely refers to
5. Depth of customer-service automation: the client's needs look simple (classify negative reviews, assist replies) - whether deeper auto-reply / human handoff is wanted is undecided

[For bidders]
State your data-source assumption explicitly: Lingxing ERP API / MCP, or SP-API plus Ads API, or report export parsing - and your fallback if entitlements are missing. **Item 13, automatic shipment creation, writes to Amazon Seller Central**: it must be human-confirmed, auditable and reversible, never unattended. Quote per module A-E and mark which items depend on client-side access being ready.
problems.title: Amazon Womenswear Store Ops Automation: Ad Monitoring, Inventory & Shipment Planning, Content Pipeline, VOC and Cost Modelling

problems.description:
[Context & goals]
Staff track X and Weibo industry activity by hand today: slow and leaky. The ask is an agent platform covering the full crawl -> analyse -> report chain. Targets: cut information-gathering time by 70%, catch an important topic within one hour, browser login only, with Q&A, subscriptions, lead discovery and one-click .docx export.
MVP: 3-5 subscribed topics; lead discovery supports multiple tasks; Q&A runs off crawled data; text and image covered end to end.

[Users & scenarios]
All internal staff, on admin-provisioned accounts, with view-level department isolation and auto-logout after 30 idle minutes. Journey: log in -> left nav switches Q&A / My Subscriptions / Lead Discovery -> read a report or create a task -> download the .docx.

[Requirements]

1 | Platform basics
- Web app, any browser, no client install
- Accounts pre-set by the admin, bound to department groups; different accounts carry different topic sets
- Reports stored permanently; the admin can configure a cleanup policy
- One-click .docx with chart snapshots and post images, named [module]_[name]_date.docx

2 | Crawling engine
- Sources: X official API v2 (developer account required); Weibo commercial data API (enterprise verification and contract required). Route not prescribed - API or otherwise
- Cleaning: on X drop pure retweets and spam accounts; on Weibo drop ad posts, giveaway retweets and troll accounts (registered under 30 days with under 10 followers, or abnormal posting frequency)

3 | Multimodal processing
- Capture: all post images (JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP) at original resolution
- Understanding: Qwen extracts OCR text, subject description and elements (people / product / logo / chart / screenshot), written back onto the post record
- Fusion: post body and image-understanding text are concatenated before analysis, so nothing in an image is lost
- Presentation: key posts show a summary plus thumbnails; the .docx embeds the images

4 | Module 1 - Q&A (basic capability is enough)
- Free-form questions over crawled text and images; RAG answers with citations; **never triggers a live crawl**
- Chat UI, Chinese input, 5 turns of context, follow-ups supported
- Allowed: summarising, counting, comparing, people analysis. Barred: code, prediction, small talk - out-of-scope gets a polite refusal
- Every assertion carries >=2 citations (author, platform, link) with image thumbnails
- When data is thin, prompt the user to create a lead-discovery task

5 | Module 2 - Topic subscription (reports must be accurate, complete)
- Topic config: keywords with AND/OR/NOT; crawl frequency hourly / 4-hourly / daily; report frequency daily or weekly, configured independently
- Sections: 1 cover (topic, date, platforms) 2 summary (~200 chars) 3 top 3 hot topics with representative posts and images 4 sentiment pie chart plus negative-post list 5 influential figures with profiles 6 post appendix (text, author, engagement, sentiment, platform, link; images on high-value posts)
- Alerting: over 50 negative posts within an hour, or a negative share above 40%, raises a top banner and is highlighted in the report. Thresholds adjustable

6 | Module 3 - Lead discovery (analysis depth required here)
- Task creation: name, keyword group, accounts (optional), platforms, look-back window (24h / 3d / 7d / 30d); "Start analysis" runs immediately
- Collection: one-shot pull over the window, deduped and cleaned as in subscriptions; progress: collecting -> image understanding -> analysing -> report ready
- Report sections: 1 overview (posts, images, accounts, time span) 2 key cohorts (top 15 by influence with profiles) 3 key posts (top 20 by engagement, 5 summarised with images) 4 sentiment pie chart 5 topic distribution (3-5 clusters) 6 DeepSeek synthesis (200-300 chars) 7 optional cross-platform comparison
- Delivery: the task list shows "completed", detail opens, .docx downloads with images; history is persistent, filterable by name and date
- Versus subscriptions: subscriptions track continuously and publish on a cycle; lead discovery is a one-shot look-back, single deliverable

7 | Visual design
- A dark, technical interface throughout, for an immersive intelligence-monitoring feel

[Technology, already chosen by the client]
- DeepSeek is the primary reasoning model: summarisation, sentiment, clustering, profiling, RAG answers, synthesis
- Qwen multimodal is the image model: OCR, image description, element recognition
- Call pattern: after ingest, call Qwen **asynchronously** for images and write results back to fields; DeepSeek then processes the full text including those results
- Deployment: domestic public cloud or internal K8s, **entire chain inside mainland China**

[For bidders]
X API v2 and the Weibo commercial API both need credentials and contracts: state who applies, how cost is billed, and the fallback while entitlements are pending (e.g. one platform first). Argue the one-hour capture target against real quotas and latency.
problems.title: SocialEye Social-Media Intelligence Agent: X / Weibo Multimodal Crawling to RAG Q&A, Topic Digests and Lead Discovery

problems.description:
[Project] "Little Dragon Tours Tongliang" — Tongliang Cultural Tourism AI Promo Film (Map Edition) | Cultural Tourism Promotion / AIGC Short Film
[Spec] Finished film approx. 106 seconds, 1920×1080, 30fps, landscape MP4

[Project] "Little Dragon Tours Tongliang" - Tongliang cultural-tourism AIGC promo film (Map Edition)
[Spec] ~106 seconds, 1920x1080, 30fps, landscape MP4 | [Budget] RMB 30,000 = approx. USD 4,440

I. Creative Core
Using the Tongliang dragon dance mascot "Little Dragon" as the first-person perspective, embodying a "tour guide" who takes viewers to check in at Tongliang's attractions, culminating in and elevated by a performance of the national intangible cultural heritage "Tongliang Fire Dragon."
Target audience: Young tourist groups, families with children, weekend short-trip travelers.
Communication goal: Shape Tongliang's cultural tourism brand image of "Thousand-Year Dragon Hometown, Fireworks of the Human World," driving check-in visits for "Weekend Trip to Tongliang" nearby tourism.
Core slogan: Head to Tongliang on the weekend — for a romantic encounter between "dragons and the human world."

II. Film Structure (Three-Part)
1) Opening Introduction 0:00–0:14: Live-action dragon dance scene cuts in; Little Dragon "leaps out" of its thousand-year dragon dance identity and transforms into a tour guide, launching the Tongliang journey;
2) Middle Tour 0:14–1:17: In map check-in format, sequentially visits Xuantian Lake, Dragon-Weaving Workshop, Tongliang Museum, and Anju Ancient Town, interspersed with hanfu costume changes and featured food experiences;
3) Climactic Ending 1:17–1:46: Little Dragon transforms into a golden beam of light flying across the night sky, arriving at the Fire Dragon performance at Xuantian Lake Plaza; the intangible heritage Fire Dragon pushes emotions to a peak, ending with a freeze-frame of a glowing map that drives home the theme.

III. Storyboard Script (10 Shots, Must Be Reproduced According to Timecodes)
1. 00:00–00:09 Dragon Dance Plaza (Live-Action Opening): Backlit sunset, courtyard red lanterns, dragon dance troupe performing with a golden giant dragon, low-angle upward shot. Voiceover (lively female voice): "I've been practicing dragon dancing for a thousand years — enough of that. Today I want to experience a new identity. Friends watching on screen, come explore all of Tongliang with me and unlock tons of hidden gem check-in spots."
2. 00:09–00:14 Xuantian Lake (Animated Transition): Cartoon Little Dragon flies over green mountains and clear waters with a golden light trail; calligraphic text "Xuantian Lake" + location pin icon. "This is Tongliang's famous scenic spot, Xuantian Lake."
3. 00:14–00:18 Xuantian Lake Shore: Little Dragon rides a glowing bicycle around the lake; family tents, picnic, parents and children eating watermelon. "Cycling around the lake by day, camping and admiring flowers, lakeside picnic."
4. 00:18–00:26 Dragon-Weaving Workshop: An old craftsman hand-weaves a dragon skeleton; Little Dragon watches; a plaque reading "Hundred-Year Tongliang Dragon-Weaving Old Craft." "This is Tongliang's inherited craft of dragon weaving — a Little Dragon was born under the old craftsman's hands."
5. 00:26–00:32 Tongliang Museum: Little Dragon passes through the "Dragon Gate" arched entrance; giant painted paper dragon, fish-shaped lantern display cases. "This is the Tongliang Museum, where you can witness Tongliang's historical development and material cultural heritage."
6. 00:32–00:43 Anju Ancient Town: Aerial shot of ancient town rooftops → stone-paved alleyways; red lanterns, oil-paper umbrellas, Sichuan opera face-changing, craftsmen, street food stalls. "The thousand-year-old Anju Ancient Town hides most of Tongliang's earthly charm. Ancient guild halls, old opera stages, century-old teahouses — every stop is a scene straight out of an ancient-style epic."
7. 00:43–01:00 Anju Ancient Town · Hanfu Shop: Little Dragon tries on hanfu and poses in front of a mirror; quick-cut Polaroid photo wall. "This hanfu is so beautiful — this dragon is naturally gifted and can't help but show it off. I absolutely must do an immersive ancient-style photo check-in."
8. 01:00–01:17 Night Market / Food Street: Little Dragon runs holding a "福" (fortune) character lantern + food montage (wooden mortar pounding rice, syrup poured over tangyuan, deep-fried snacks). "All that photo-taking made me hungry — I'm diving into Tongliang's specialty foods! Anju Hanlin Crisp, Tongliang Marinated Phoenix Claws, Chongchong Cake… so delicious I just can't stop. No more talking — time to eat!"
9. 01:17–01:25 Transition · Night Alley: Little Dragon looks up alertly and transforms into a golden beam of light shooting through the night alleyway. "Oh no, the molten iron flower performance is about to start — this dragon needs to get back on track."
10. 01:25–01:46 Xuantian Lake Plaza (Grand Finale): Golden light trail leaps over the lake and mountains; bare-chested dancers wield fire dragons, sparks cascade like a waterfall, lake reflections and cheering crowd; ending freeze-frame on a glowing Tongliang map. Male voice (deep and resonant): "The national intangible cultural heritage — Tongliang Fire Dragon. Thousand-year dragon hometown, fireworks of the human world. Head to Tongliang on the weekend, for a romantic encounter between dragons and the human world."

IV. List of Attractions and Cultural Elements
· Xuantian Lake: Cycling around the lake, camping and flower-viewing, lakeside picnic (families/family tents); the "Xuantian Lake Plaza" at the film's end is the main venue for the Fire Dragon night performance (aerial shot of lake reflections + audience silhouettes).
· Dragon-Weaving Workshop: Tongliang's hundred-year intangible cultural heritage dragon-weaving craft; old craftsman hand-weaving a dragon skeleton, dim workshop lighting, "Hundred-Year Tongliang Dragon-Weaving Old Craft" plaque; narratively echoes Little Dragon's origins.
· Tongliang Museum: "Dragon Gate" arched entrance, giant painted paper dragon, fish-shaped lanterns, and other exhibits.
· Anju Ancient Town: Aerial shot of rooftops + stone-paved alleyways; red lanterns, oil-paper umbrellas, ancient guild halls, old opera stages, century-old teahouses, Sichuan opera face-changing, craftsmen, street butcher stalls; hanfu costume immersive ancient-style photo check-in (pink skirt and flower crown, scholar's robe and folding fan, Polaroid photo wall quick-cut).
· Tongliang Specialty Foods: Anju Hanlin Crisp, Tongliang Marinated Phoenix Claws, Chongchong Cake, and other street snacks; "Authentic Tongliang Jianghu Flavors" food montage quick-cut.
· Tongliang Fire Dragon (Grand Finale): National intangible cultural heritage, Xuantian Lake Plaza night performance, sparks cascading like a waterfall.

V. Production Requirements
1) IP Character Consistency: The cartoon Little Dragon (golden body, orange-red mane, gem embedded in forehead) runs throughout the entire film; AI generation must strictly maintain consistent character traits;
2) Live-Action + AIGC Integration: Key scenes such as dragon dance, fire dragon, and ancient town alleyways use live-action footage to ensure authentic impact; virtual scenes are generated by AI text-to-image / image-to-video; AI characters must be naturally composited into live-action scenes (e.g., Little Dragon in the same frame as tourists, watching dragon-weaving at the workshop);
3) Voice-Over: AI voice-over; main lively female voice + deep male voice at the ending;
4) Music: Electronic guofeng style, with progressive emotional escalation by segment (upbeat electronic → erhu and guzheng → solemn orchestral → flute and pipa → pop electronic → folk music hip-hop → epic symphonic);
5) Map Edition Packaging: Each attraction's appearance is accompanied by calligraphic place-name labels + location pin icons (Xuantian Lake / Dragon-Weaving Workshop / Tongliang Museum / Anju Ancient Town / Xuantian Lake Plaza), with a freeze-frame of a glowing Tongliang map at the end;
6) Subtitles: Yellow-outlined decorative characters presented sentence by sentence, synchronized with the voiceover;
7) Sound Effects: Shutter sounds, chewing sound effects, spark crackle sounds, crowd cheers, and other accents;
8) Review Compliance: Attraction information, intangible heritage descriptions, and food names must be verified for accuracy; material copyright and music licensing must be clear; AIGC label added throughout the film.

VI. Deliverables List
① Finished Film: 1920×1080 MP4, approx. 106 seconds, with subtitles, music, and voiceover;
② Vertical Screen Adaptation: 9:16 short video platform version (as needed);
③ Storyboard Script: Complete script table with timecodes, visuals, subtitles, and voiceover;
④ Attraction Asset List: Categorized archive of live-action and AI-generated assets;
⑤ AIGC Compliance Statement: AI-generated content labeling and copyright documentation.

problems.description:
Given one day of multi-source financial news, produce the ranked top 10 EVENTS and a genuinely distinct short-video script for each.

Two things have already been tried and rejected on a previous run of this task, so read these before bidding:

A previous delivery clustered correctly but wrote the SAME paragraph for all 10 scripts, describing its own dedup methodology instead of the news. Every script read: 'Multiple articles about the same underlying event were grouped before ranking...' A viewer learned nothing about what actually happened. That is a fail, no matter how good the clustering is.

The same delivery cited all 10 sources as tinyurl.com short links. The point of a source link is that a reader can verify the claim; a shortener removes that.

Buyer: ClawHunt (self-funded). Derived from a real client requirement.
